record.original_question: Can one explicitly compute, program, and publish tables of parity-independent osp(1|2) 6-j^S symbols for low spins (for example up to spin 20) from the general formulas cited by the paper, so that low-spin calculations can test candidate triangle-sum-rule identities and reveal patterns among the expansion coefficients x?

evidence.quote: The best should be to try doing hand-calculations for low values of spins occuring in 6-j^S symbols (up to 20 for example).

These tables have neither been programmed nor published up today. For any interested and motivated searcher / programmer, this task could be rapidly carried out from our general formulas given in ref. [5].
That could furnish an invaluable help not only for the problem under study but certainly also in other areas of the physics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ denote the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra of rank one, whose finite-dimensional irreducible representations are labelled by a non-negative half-integer "superspin" $S$. For any six superspins $(S_1,S_2,S_3,S_4,S_5,S_6)$ satisfying the relevant triangular conditions, one has well-defined parity-independent $6\text{-}j^S$ symbols
$$\begin{Bmatrix} S_1 & S_2 & S_3 \\ S_4 & S_5 & S_6 \end{Bmatrix}_{\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)},$$
which are the recoupling coefficients for tensor products of three irreducible $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-modules, defined by closed-form general formulas analogous to the Racah formula for $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ $6$-$j$ symbols.

The task is the following:

(a) Using the known general closed-form expressions, produce explicit numerical (or exact rational/algebraic) tables of all parity-independent $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ $6\text{-}j^S$ symbols whose six entries are superspins bounded by $20$ (i.e. $S_i \in \{0, \tfrac{1}{2}, 1, \tfrac{3}{2}, \dots, 20\}$ for $i=1,\dots,6$, subject to the appropriate triangle constraints).

(b) Use these tabulated values to test candidate triangle-sum-rule identities of the form
$$\sum_{S} (\text{weight}(S)) \begin{Bmatrix} \cdots \end{Bmatrix}_{\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)} \begin{Bmatrix} \cdots \end{Bmatrix}_{\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)} = \text{(closed expression)},$$
analogous to the Biedenharn–Elliott and Racah sum rules for $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and to determine whether the expansion coefficients $x$ that appear in such identities exhibit recognisable closed-form patterns (rational, factorial, or hypergeometric).

Concretely: produce the tables, identify the triangle-sum-rule identities for $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ that they verify, and characterise the resulting expansion coefficients.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface any published or programmed tables of parity-independent osp(1|2) 6-j^S symbols up to spin 20, nor a verified set of triangle-sum-rule identities with characterised expansion coefficients. While general closed-form expressions for osp(1|2) 6-j symbols are known in the literature, no source confirms that the tabulation and pattern-identification task has been carried out. The status is therefore unknown.

status_evidence.title: 6-j symbol - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General reference on 6-j symbols and recoupling theory; no mention of computed osp(1|2) parity-independent tables.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references describe 6-j symbols generally but do not document computed osp(1|2) parity-independent tables up to spin 20.

status_evidence.title: An elementary approach to 6j-symbols
status_evidence.snippet: Treats classical, quantum, rational, trigonometric, and elliptic 6j-symbols; does not provide osp(1|2) tabulated values.
status_evidence.claim: Existing surveys of 6j-symbol variants do not include the requested osp(1|2) tabulation.
